offense_class: Gross Misdemeanor (first/second/third); Class B Felony (fourth+ within 10 years or prior vehicular homicide/assault)
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle within Washington
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor, marijuana, or any drug
Or had a BAC of .08 or higher within two hours after driving
Or had a THC concentration of 5.00 ng/mL or higher within two hours after driving
mandatory_minimum: 24 consecutive hours imprisonment and $350 fine (first offense); 30 days imprisonment and $500 fine (second within 7 years)
enhancements: BAC .15 or higher or refusal of test (enhanced mandatory minimums under RCW § 46.61.5055)
Prior vehicular homicide or vehicular assault conviction (Class B Felony)
Fourth or subsequent offense within 10 years (Class B Felony)
notes: Implied consent under RCW § 46.20.308. Admin license suspension 90 days first offense. Ignition interlock required. 24/7 sobriety program monitoring may be ordered.

elements: Defendant drove a vehicle within Washington
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor, marijuana, or any drug
BAC .08 or higher or THC 5.00 ng/mL or higher within two hours after driving
No prior DUI convictions within 7 years
mandatory_minimum: 24 consecutive hours imprisonment; $350 fine; 90-day license suspension; ignition interlock device for 1 year
enhancements: BAC .15 or higher (48 hours mandatory minimum; $500 fine)
Refusal of breath/blood test (48 hours mandatory minimum; $500 fine)
notes: Eligible for deferred prosecution under RCW § 10.05. Must complete alcohol/drug assessment. Ignition interlock required for license reinstatement.

offense_class: Gross Misdemeanor (second/third); Class B Felony (fourth+ within 10 years)
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle within Washington
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor, marijuana, or any drug
BAC .08 or higher or THC 5.00 ng/mL or higher within two hours after driving
One or more prior DUI convictions within 7 years (misdemeanor) or 10 years (felony)
mandatory_minimum: 30 days imprisonment and $500 fine (second); 90 days imprisonment and $1,000 fine (third); 364 days imprisonment and $1,000 fine (fourth+)
enhancements: Refusal of breath/blood test (enhanced mandatory minimums)
Prior vehicular homicide or vehicular assault conviction
notes: Second offense: 2-year license revocation. Third: 3-year revocation. Fourth+ felony: permanent revocation possible. Ignition interlock required for all repeat offenders.

offense_class: Gross Misdemeanor; Class B Felony (fourth+ within 10 years)
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle within Washington
While under the influence of any drug
Or under the combined influence of alcohol and any drug
THC per se limit: 5.00 ng/mL; no per se limit for other drugs
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
notes: Washington has a per se THC limit of 5.00 ng/mL. For other drugs, prosecution must prove actual impairment. Includes prescription medications that impair driving.

elements: Defendant drove any vehicle
In willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Common plea-down from DUI. 30-day license suspension. Reckless endangerment under RCW § 9A.36.050 is a separate gross misdemeanor.

statute_title: Duty to Stop — Accident Involving Injury or Death
offense_class: Class C Felony (injury); Class B Felony (death)
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury or death of any person
Defendant failed to stop at the scene
Defendant failed to give name, address, insurance information, and render aid
enhancements: Hit-and-run with property damage only is a misdemeanor under RCW § 46.52.010
notes: Property damage only hit-and-run is a misdemeanor. Attended vehicle hit-and-run is a gross misdemeanor. License revocation upon conviction.

elements: Defendant operated or drove a motor vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs, or recklessly, or with disregard for the safety of others
Proximately caused the death of another person
enhancements: DUI-related vehicular homicide has aggravating sentencing factors
notes: Vehicular homicide is a Class A Felony regardless of whether caused by DUI, reckless driving, or disregard for safety. Standard sentencing range depends on offender score.

elements: Defendant operated or drove a motor vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs, or recklessly, or with disregard for the safety of others
Caused substantial bodily harm to another person
notes: Washington does not have a separate vehicular manslaughter statute. Vehicular assault under RCW § 46.61.522 covers non-fatal serious injuries. Deaths are charged as vehicular homicide.

statute_title: Driving While License Suspended or Revoked
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle
Defendant's license was suspended or revoked
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension or revocation
enhancements: First degree (DUI-related suspension) has mandatory minimum jail
notes: DWLS 1st degree (DUI-related) is most serious. DWLS 3rd degree for administrative suspensions (unpaid tickets, etc.) is a simple misdemeanor.

statute_title: Attempting to Elude a Police Vehicle
elements: A uniformed police officer signaled the defendant to stop
Signal was given by hand, voice, emergency light, or siren
Defendant willfully failed or refused to stop
Defendant attempted to elude the pursuing police vehicle
notes: Attempting to elude is always a felony in Washington regardless of the underlying stop reason. Spike strips and pursuit intervention techniques authorized.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled substance
Substance is listed in Schedules I through V
Defendant did not have a valid prescription
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense after July 1, 2023 (up to 364 days)
notes: Washington passed the Blake fix in 2023 (SB 5536) making simple possession a gross misdemeanor. Prosecutors encouraged to divert first/second offenses to assessment and treatment. Cannabis legal for 21+ under RCW § 69.50.360.

statute_title: Possession of Marijuana — Over Legal Limit or Under 21
elements: Defendant possessed useable marijuana, concentrates, or infused products
Amount exceeded legal limits (1 oz useable, 7g concentrate, 16 oz infused solid, 72 oz infused liquid)
Or defendant was under 21 years of age
notes: Recreational cannabis legal for 21+ since 2012 (I-502). Possession within legal limits is not a crime. Over-limit possession or under-21 possession remains prosecutable.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Defendant did not have a valid prescription
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense (up to 364 days)
notes: Under 2023 Blake fix, simple cocaine possession is a gross misdemeanor. Diversion to treatment encouraged for first/second offenses.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Defendant did not have a valid prescription
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense (up to 364 days)
notes: Under 2023 Blake fix, simple meth possession is a gross misdemeanor. Manufacturing methamphetamine remains a Class B Felony under RCW § 69.50.401.

statute_title: Manufacture or Delivery of Controlled Substance — Narcotic/Schedule I-II
elements: Defendant manufactured, delivered, or possessed with intent to deliver
A controlled substance classified as a narcotic from Schedule I or II
Including heroin, cocaine, methamphetamine, or fentanyl
enhancements: Within 1,000 feet of school, school bus stop, public park, or housing project
notes: Sentencing depends on offender score under Sentencing Reform Act. School zone enhancement adds 24 months. Delivery to a minor is a separate Class A Felony.

offense_class: Class C Felony (Schedule III-V); Class B Felony (Schedule I-II non-narcotic)
elements: Defendant delivered or possessed with intent to deliver
A non-narcotic controlled substance
From Schedule I through V
enhancements: Within 1,000 feet of school or public park
notes: Non-narcotic Schedule I-II (e.g., amphetamines, hallucinogens) is Class B Felony. Schedule III-V is Class C Felony.

offense_class: Class B Felony (Schedule I-II); Class C Felony (Schedule III-V)
elements: Defendant manufactured a controlled substance
Manufacturing includes production, preparation, compounding, or processing
Substance is listed in Schedules I through V
enhancements: Clandestine lab near residence with children present
notes: Manufacturing methamphetamine carries additional cleanup costs. If children present, child endangerment charges also apply.

statute_title: Use or Delivery of Drug Paraphernalia
elements: Defendant used or delivered drug paraphernalia
Knowing that it would be used to plant, propagate, manufacture, or consume a controlled substance
enhancements: Delivery to a person under 18 (gross misdemeanor)
notes: Personal use paraphernalia is a misdemeanor. Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor is enhanced. Paraphernalia for cannabis use by adults 21+ is legal.

statute_title: Possession with Intent to Manufacture or Deliver
offense_class: Class B Felony (Schedule I-II narcotic); Class C Felony (Schedule III-V)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
With intent to manufacture or deliver
Intent may be inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, or other indicia
enhancements: School zone enhancement (within 1,000 feet of school)
notes: Distinct from simple possession. Prosecution must prove intent through circumstantial evidence — quantity, packaging, communications, cash.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
With premeditated intent to cause death
Or during the commission of a felony (felony murder)
mandatory_minimum: Life imprisonment with minimum term set by Indeterminate Sentence Review Board
enhancements: Aggravating factors under RCW § 10.95.020 (death penalty abolished 2018; LWOP possible)
notes: Washington abolished the death penalty in 2018 (State v. Gregory). Maximum sentence is life without parole. Mandatory minimum is life with possibility of parole.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
With intent to cause death but without premeditation
Or during commission of a felony (non-enumerated felony murder)
notes: Standard sentencing range varies by offender score. Firearm and deadly weapon enhancements apply.

elements: Defendant recklessly caused the death of another person
Or intentionally and unlawfully killed an unborn quick child by inflicting injury upon the mother
notes: Manslaughter 1 in Washington is analogous to voluntary manslaughter in other states. Covers reckless killings and heat-of-passion killings.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Through criminal negligence
notes: Manslaughter 2 covers criminally negligent homicides. Lower culpability than reckless manslaughter 1.

elements: Defendant assaulted another person
With intent to inflict great bodily harm
With a firearm or deadly weapon or force likely to produce great bodily harm or death
notes: Assault 1 is the most serious assault charge in Washington. Classified as a strike offense under the Persistent Offender Accountability Act.

offense_class: Gross Misdemeanor; Class C Felony (against certain protected persons)
elements: Defendant assaulted another person
Assault not amounting to assault in the first, second, or third degree
enhancements: Domestic violence designation (mandatory arrest under RCW § 10.31.100)
Against first responder, transit operator, or school employee (Class C Felony)
notes: Assault 4 is the catch-all assault charge. Domestic violence assault 4 triggers mandatory arrest, no-contact orders, and firearms surrender.

elements: Defendant intentionally assaulted another and recklessly inflicted substantial bodily harm
Or assaulted another with a deadly weapon
Or assaulted another by strangulation or suffocation
notes: Washington does not have a separate battery statute. Assault 2 covers what other states classify as felony battery. Strangulation added as a qualifying act.

elements: Defendant unlawfully took personal property from the person or in the presence of another
Against that person's will
By use or threatened use of immediate force, violence, or fear of injury
notes: Robbery 2 is the base robbery charge. Robbery 1 (RCW § 9A.56.200) involves deadly weapons, injury, or financial institution.

elements: Defendant committed robbery
While armed with a deadly weapon or displaying what appeared to be a firearm
Or inflicted bodily injury
Or committed robbery of a financial institution
notes: Strike offense under the Persistent Offender Accountability Act (three strikes). Firearm enhancement is mandatory and runs consecutive to base sentence.

elements: Defendant intentionally abducted another person
With intent to hold for ransom, use as a shield or hostage, facilitate a felony, or inflict bodily injury
Or abducted a person under 16 years of age
notes: Kidnapping 2 (RCW § 9A.40.030) is a Class B Felony for intentional abduction with intent to facilitate other offenses. Unlawful imprisonment is a Class C Felony.

elements: Defendant knowingly and maliciously caused a fire or explosion
Which damaged a dwelling
Or which damaged any structure or property when another person was present
notes: Arson 2 (RCW § 9A.48.030) is a Class B Felony for non-dwelling structures. Reckless burning (RCW § 9A.48.040) is a Class C Felony.

statute_title: Attempted Murder in the First Degree
elements: Defendant took a substantial step toward committing murder in the first degree
With premeditated intent to cause the death of another person
Act went beyond mere preparation
notes: Attempted murder is punished one seriousness level below the completed offense. Attempted murder 2 is also a Class A Felony.

statute_title: Assault in the Second Degree — Deadly Weapon
elements: Defendant assaulted another person
With a deadly weapon
Deadly weapon includes any instrument likely to produce death or substantial bodily harm
notes: Assault with a deadly weapon is charged as Assault 2 in Washington. If great bodily harm intended with a deadly weapon, may be charged as Assault 1.

elements: Defendant committed theft of property or services
Value exceeds $5,000
Or property taken from the person of another
enhancements: Theft from a vulnerable adult (additional penalties)
notes: Washington uses a three-tier theft system: 1st ($5,000+), 2nd ($750-$5,000), 3rd (under $750).

elements: Defendant committed theft of property or services
Value exceeds $750 but does not exceed $5,000
notes: Theft 2 threshold is $750. Washington does not use the term 'grand theft' — equivalent is theft in the first or second degree.

elements: Defendant committed theft of property or services
Value does not exceed $750
notes: Equivalent to petty theft in other states. Retailers may also pursue civil penalties of $100-$650 plus retail value.

elements: Defendant committed theft of retail merchandise
With special circumstances: organized retail theft, theft with accomplices, or use of tools to defeat security
enhancements: Use of devices to overcome security measures
notes: Standard shoplifting is charged as theft 1/2/3 depending on value. Retail theft with special circumstances is an enhanced felony charge for organized or sophisticated theft.

elements: Defendant entered or remained unlawfully in a building
Other than a vehicle or dwelling
With intent to commit a crime against a person or property therein
notes: Burglary 2 covers commercial buildings. Burglary 1 (residential) is a Class A Felony and a strike offense.

elements: Defendant entered or remained unlawfully in a dwelling
Other than a vehicle
With intent to commit a crime against a person or property therein
notes: Residential burglary is a strike offense under the Persistent Offender Accountability Act. Separate from Burglary 1 (RCW § 9A.52.020) which requires additional elements.

elements: Defendant committed theft of a motor vehicle
notes: Motor vehicle theft is always a Class B Felony regardless of vehicle value. Possession of a stolen vehicle (RCW § 9A.56.068) is a Class B Felony if value exceeds $5,000.

statute_title: Possessing Stolen Property in the First Degree
elements: Defendant knowingly received, retained, possessed, or disposed of stolen property
Value exceeds $5,000
Or property is a firearm or motor vehicle
notes: Possessing Stolen Property 2 (RCW § 9A.56.150) is Class C Felony ($750-$5,000). PSP 3 is gross misdemeanor (under $750).

statute_title: Malicious Mischief in the First Degree
elements: Defendant knowingly and maliciously caused physical damage to property of another
In an amount exceeding $5,000
notes: Malicious mischief 2 ($750-$5,000) is Class C Felony. Malicious mischief 3 (under $750) is gross misdemeanor.

statute_title: Criminal Trespass in the First Degree
elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully in a building
notes: Criminal trespass 2 (RCW § 9A.52.080) — entering or remaining on premises — is a misdemeanor.

statute_title: Malicious Mischief in the Third Degree
elements: Defendant knowingly and maliciously caused physical damage to property of another
Value under $750
notes: Washington uses 'malicious mischief' rather than 'criminal mischief.' Three tiers based on damage value.

statute_title: Domestic Violence — Assault in the Fourth Degree
elements: Defendant committed an assault against a family or household member
Family/household member includes spouse, former spouse, persons with a child in common, cohabitants, or dating relationship
enhancements: Strangulation (elevated to Assault 2 — Class B Felony)
notes: DV is a designation, not a separate crime. Mandatory arrest policy under RCW § 10.31.100. Firearms surrender required. No-contact order issued automatically.

statute_title: Domestic Violence — Assault in the Second Degree
elements: Defendant assaulted a family or household member
And recklessly inflicted substantial bodily harm
Or assaulted by strangulation or suffocation
notes: DV Assault 2 carries the DV designation with all associated consequences. Felony DV triggers federal firearms prohibition under 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(9).

statute_title: Criminal Mistreatment in the Third Degree
elements: Defendant was the parent, guardian, or person with a duty of care
Defendant recklessly created an imminent and substantial risk of bodily harm to a child
enhancements: Resulting in bodily harm (Criminal Mistreatment 2 — Class C Felony)
Resulting in great bodily harm or death (Criminal Mistreatment 1 — Class B Felony)
notes: Washington uses 'criminal mistreatment' rather than 'child endangerment.' Degrees based on resulting harm.

statute_title: Assault of a Child in the First Degree
elements: Defendant, being 18 years or older, committed assault in the first degree against a child under 13
Or intentionally assaulted a child and caused great bodily harm
notes: Strike offense. Assault of a Child 2 (RCW § 9A.36.130) is Class B Felony. Assault of a Child 3 (RCW § 9A.36.140) is Class C Felony.

offense_class: Gross Misdemeanor (first); Class C Felony (two or more prior violations)
elements: A valid protection or no-contact order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant willfully violated the order
enhancements: Two or more prior violations (Class C Felony)
notes: Washington consolidated protection order statutes under RCW 7.105 effective July 2022. Violation with assault may be charged as both crimes.

elements: Defendant intentionally and repeatedly harassed or followed another person
The person being stalked was placed in fear of injury to person or property
Defendant intended to frighten, intimidate, or harass the person
The stalking occurred without lawful authority
enhancements: Stalking in violation of a protection order (Class B Felony)
Stalking same victim as prior conviction (Class B Felony)
notes: Cyberstalking under RCW § 9.61.260 is a separate gross misdemeanor. Aggravated stalking enhancers elevate to Class B Felony.

offense_class: Gross Misdemeanor; Class C Felony (threat to kill)
elements: Defendant knowingly threatened to cause bodily injury to another person
Or to physically damage another's property
Words or conduct placed the person threatened in reasonable fear
enhancements: Against criminal justice participant or witness (Class C Felony)
notes: Felony harassment includes death threats. Telephone harassment under RCW § 9.61.230 is a separate gross misdemeanor.

statute_title: Criminal Mistreatment in the First Degree — Vulnerable Adult
elements: Defendant was a person with a duty of care for a vulnerable adult
Defendant caused great bodily harm by withholding basic necessities of life
Or recklessly caused great bodily harm
notes: Vulnerable adult includes elderly and dependent adults. Criminal mistreatment 2 is Class C Felony. Theft from a vulnerable adult carries additional penalties.

offense_class: Class B Felony (convicted felon); Class C Felony (certain misdemeanants)
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant was prohibited from possessing firearms under state or federal law
enhancements: Possession during commission of another felony
notes: Prohibited persons include convicted felons, persons committed for mental health treatment, persons subject to protection orders, and persons convicted of certain DV offenses.

statute_title: Unlawful Possession of Firearm — First Degree (Felon)
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant had previously been convicted of a serious offense as defined in RCW § 9.41.010
enhancements: Possession of firearm during commission of felony
notes: Serious offenses include murder, robbery, rape, assault 1 or 2, kidnapping, and controlled substance felonies. Any prior felony conviction is a Class C Felony under second degree.

elements: Defendant carried a concealed pistol without a valid concealed pistol license
Or carried a loaded pistol in a vehicle without a valid CPL
notes: Washington requires a concealed pistol license (CPL) for carrying concealed. Open carry of rifles/shotguns is generally legal. CPL issued by local law enforcement.

offense_class: Gross Misdemeanor; Class C Felony (if injury results)
elements: Defendant aimed a firearm at a human being
Or willfully discharged a firearm in a manner that endangered others
notes: Separate from drive-by shooting (RCW § 9A.36.045) which is a Class B Felony.

statute_title: Identity Theft in the First Degree
elements: Defendant knowingly obtained, possessed, used, or transferred a means of identification of another person
With intent to commit or aid any crime
And obtained credit, money, goods, services, or anything of value exceeding $1,500
notes: Identity theft 2 (under $1,500) is Class C Felony. RCW § 9.35.020 also covers synthetic identity fraud.

offense_class: Class B Felony ($5,000+); Class C Felony ($750-$5,000); Gross Misdemeanor (under $750)
penalty_max: 10 years (Class B); 5 years (Class C); 364 days (gross misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant was entrusted with property of another
Defendant wrongfully converted the property to own use
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Washington does not have a separate embezzlement statute. Embezzlement is prosecuted as theft under the general theft statutes.

elements: Defendant falsely made, completed, or altered a written instrument
Or possessed a forged instrument with knowledge it was forged
With intent to injure or defraud
notes: Written instruments include checks, contracts, deeds, public records, prescriptions. Separate from criminal impersonation (RCW § 9A.60.040).

offense_class: Varies by amount: Class B Felony ($5,000+); Class C Felony ($750-$5,000); Gross Misdemeanor (under $750)
penalty_max: 10 years (Class B); 5 years (Class C); 364 days (gross misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant obtained property or services of another
By means of deception, false representation, or false pretenses
With intent to deprive
notes: Fraud is prosecuted under theft by deception provisions. Specific fraud statutes also exist for insurance fraud, securities fraud, and mortgage fraud.

statute_title: Theft of a Credit Card or Access Device
elements: Defendant obtained a credit or debit card or access device of another without consent
Or received a card knowing it was obtained unlawfully
With intent to use, sell, or transfer
notes: Includes access device fraud. Use of a stolen or forged credit card may also be charged as identity theft or theft by deception.

fine_max: $20,000 or twice the value of the property involved
elements: Defendant conducted a financial transaction
Knowing the property involved was proceeds of specified unlawful activity
With intent to promote the carrying on of specified unlawful activity
notes: Money laundering includes structuring transactions to avoid reporting requirements. Forfeiture of laundered property authorized.

elements: Defendant engaged in sexual intercourse with another person
By forcible compulsion
Or when the victim was incapable of consent by reason of physical or mental incapacity
notes: Washington uses 'rape' rather than 'sexual assault' for its most serious sexual offenses. Sex offender registration required.

elements: Defendant engaged in sexual intercourse with another person by forcible compulsion
And used or threatened use of a deadly weapon
Or kidnapped the victim
Or inflicted serious physical injury
Or feloniously entered the building where the victim was situated
enhancements: Strike offense under three strikes law
notes: Rape 1 is a strike offense. Indeterminate sentencing with minimum term set by Indeterminate Sentence Review Board. Lifetime sex offender registration.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Gross Misdemeanor (if victim under 14); Class C Felony (prior conviction)
elements: Defendant intentionally made an open and obscene exposure of person
Or of another person
Knowing that such conduct was likely to cause reasonable affront or alarm
enhancements: Prior indecent exposure conviction (Class C Felony)
notes: Felony indecent exposure requires a prior conviction. Sex offender registration may be required for felony indecent exposure.

elements: Defendant paid or agreed to pay a fee to another person
For the purpose of engaging in sexual conduct
enhancements: Patronizing a minor (Class C Felony under RCW § 9.68A.100)
notes: Promoting prostitution (RCW § 9A.88.070) is a Class C Felony. Trafficking of persons for sex (RCW § 9A.40.100) is a Class A Felony.

elements: Defendant aided, invited, employed, or caused a minor to engage in sexually explicit conduct
Knowing the minor was under 18 years of age
notes: Possession of child pornography (RCW § 9.68A.070) is a Class B Felony. Dealing in depictions of a minor (RCW § 9.68A.050) is a Class B Felony.

statute_title: Failure to Register as a Sex Offender
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender
Defendant knowingly failed to register or update registration as required
notes: Registration requirements under RCW § 9A.44.130. Must register within 3 business days of release or relocation.

offense_class: Class A Felony (first/second degree); Class C Felony (third degree)
elements: Defendant had sexual intercourse with a child
First degree: victim under 12, defendant 24 months+ older
Second degree: victim 12-14, defendant 36 months+ older
Third degree: victim 14-16, defendant 48 months+ older
notes: Washington uses 'rape of a child' rather than 'statutory rape.' First and second degree are strike offenses. Age gaps determine the degree.

elements: Defendant intentionally disrupted any lawful assembly or meeting of persons
Or obstructed vehicular or pedestrian traffic without lawful authority
Or engaged in fighting or tumultuous behavior
notes: Failure to disperse (RCW § 9A.84.020) is a separate misdemeanor. Riot (RCW § 9A.84.010) is a Class C Felony.

elements: A person authorized to make an arrest was making a lawful arrest
Defendant intentionally prevented or attempted to prevent the arrest
By using or threatening to use physical force or violence
notes: Separate from obstructing a law enforcement officer. Use of force against an officer during arrest may support additional assault charges.

elements: Defendant knowingly hindered, delayed, or obstructed
A law enforcement officer in the discharge of official duties
notes: Does not require physical force — verbal obstruction or providing false information sufficient. Separate from making a false statement (RCW § 9A.76.175).

elements: Defendant engaged in intentional disobedience of a court order
Or disorderly, contemptuous, or insolent behavior toward the court
notes: Punitive contempt requires proof beyond a reasonable doubt. Remedial (civil) contempt uses coercive sanctions to compel compliance.

offense_class: Not a criminal offense in Washington
elements: Person is intoxicated in a public place
And is a danger to self or others
notes: Washington decriminalized public intoxication. Intoxicated persons are taken to a treatment facility or shelter, not jail. Disorderly conduct may be charged if behavior is disruptive.

offense_class: Class A Felony (if underlying is Class A); Class B Felony (if underlying is Class B/C); Gross Misdemeanor (if underlying is misdemeanor)
penalty_max: Life (Class A); 10 years (Class B); 364 days (gross misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant was released by court order on bail or personal recognizance
Defendant knowingly failed to appear as required
For any court hearing in connection with a charged crime
notes: Bail jumping severity matches the underlying charge level. Washington uses 'bail jumping' rather than 'failure to appear.'

statute_title: Making a False or Misleading Statement to a Public Servant
elements: Defendant knowingly made a false or misleading material statement
To a public servant in connection with an investigation or official proceeding
notes: Filing a false police report falls under this statute. Separate from perjury (which requires an oath).

offense_class: Gross Misdemeanor; Class C Felony (death threat)
elements: Defendant knowingly threatened to cause bodily injury immediately or in the future
To the person threatened or to any other person
Threat placed the person in reasonable fear it would be carried out
notes: Washington calls this 'harassment' rather than 'criminal threats.' Death threats elevate to felony. Includes threats via electronic communication.

elements: Defendant made a materially false statement
While under oath in an official proceeding
Defendant knew the statement was false
notes: Perjury 2 (RCW § 9A.72.030) is Class C Felony for false written statements under oath. False swearing (RCW § 9A.72.040) is gross misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant offered, conferred, or agreed to confer a benefit
Upon a public servant
With intent to influence the public servant's official actions
notes: Receiving a bribe (RCW § 9A.68.020) is also a Class B Felony. Includes commercial bribery under RCW § 9A.68.060.

elements: Defendant escaped from custody or a detention facility
While being detained for a felony charge or conviction
notes: Escape 2 (RCW § 9A.76.120) is Class C Felony for misdemeanor detainees. Escape 3 (RCW § 9A.76.130) is gross misdemeanor for community custody violations.

statute_title: Animal Cruelty in the First Degree
elements: Defendant intentionally inflicted substantial pain on, caused physical injury to, or killed an animal
By a means causing undue suffering
notes: Animal cruelty 2 (RCW § 16.52.207) is a gross misdemeanor for negligent mistreatment. Felony animal cruelty may trigger mental health evaluation.

offense_class: Varies — up to 60 days confinement per violation; full sentence for revocation
elements: Defendant was on community custody or supervised probation
Defendant violated a condition of supervision
notes: Washington uses 'community custody' rather than 'probation.' Graduated sanctions: 3 days first, 15 days second, 30 days third. New crime may trigger revocation of full sentence.

offense_class: Varies — return to prison for remaining term
elements: Defendant was released on parole by the Indeterminate Sentence Review Board
Defendant violated a condition of parole
notes: Washington largely replaced parole with community custody under the Sentencing Reform Act of 1981. Parole still applies to pre-SRA sentences and certain indeterminate sentences.

elements: Defendant solicited, commanded, encouraged, or requested another person to commit a crime
Or aided or agreed to aid another person in planning or committing a crime
With knowledge that it would promote or facilitate the commission of the crime
notes: An accomplice is punished as a principal. Mere presence at the scene or knowledge of the crime is not sufficient. Must show intentional participation.

offense_class: One class lower than the target offense (Class B if target is Class A; Class C if target is Class B; Gross Misdemeanor if target is Class C)
penalty_max: One grade below target offense maximum
elements: Defendant had intent to commit a specific crime
Defendant took a substantial step toward commission of the crime
Substantial step must be conduct strongly corroborative of criminal intent
notes: Attempt is graded one class below the target offense. Abandonment is an affirmative defense if voluntary and complete.

offense_class: Same class as the target offense
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to engage in conduct constituting a crime
Defendant or co-conspirator took a substantial step in furtherance of the agreement
notes: Unlike federal conspiracy, Washington conspiracy requires an overt act. Conspiracy is punished at the same level as the target offense, not one grade below.
